Post-fledging, juveniles remain dependent on parental care for an additional several weeks as they refine their foraging skills and learn to recognize suitable food items. Field studies suggest that adult survival rates are moderately high, which is consistent with a strategy that prioritizes individual persistence over high annual fecundity.
